sections.subtitle: Zadružna banka koja nije prošla, Litva koja je uspjela i europski strah od neuspjeha
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj priča o tri neuspjela pokušaja osnivanja zadružne banke i o Litvi kao fintech hubu
sections.content:
Voditelj nudi opipljiv kontraprimjer hrvatske prakse. Najveća hrvatska zadruga, priča, u tri je navrata pokušala pred HNB-om osnovati banku u kojoj bi vlasnici bili sami članovi i u kojoj ne bi bilo ekstrakcije iz ekonomije — i to nije bilo moguće.

Isti ti ljudi, nastavlja, danas to isto rade preko **Centralne banke Litve**, koja se za vrijeme korone svjesno pozicionirala kao *fintech hub* i pozvala sve da dođu k njoj. Iz te je jurisdikcije, podsjeća, izrastao i Revolut, koji se proširio cijelom Europom i nakon niza godina postao profitabilan — dokazujući usput da SEPA transakcije mogu biti besplatne.

Marijana Šarolić Robić u tome vidi upravo ono što gura cijela tržišta naprijed: netko dovoljno hrabar, pionir koji se usudi takvu stvar podržati. Time uvodi pojam o kojem, kaže, govori i europska povjerenica za start-upove — **„license to fail"**.

Problem je, tvrdi, u europskom mentalitetu:

- u Europi je **propast sramota**, stečaj je sramota, a neuspjeh donosi gubitak prestiža, društvenog ugleda i reputacije te ogovaranje „na najnižoj razini";
- u Americi te, suprotno, pitaju koliko si puta propao prije nego što ulože u tebe — jer to znači da se znaš dići s koljena;
- serijski poduzetnik nije onaj koji je napravio četiri exita, nego onaj koji se zna izvući iz svake situacije.

Zato zagovara liberalizaciju te paradigme: da bude dopušteno eksperimentirati, padati, dizati se, „zaribati", naučiti i ići dalje — te da se Europa, a unutar nje i Hrvatska, pozicionira kao mjesto gdje je inoviranje **društveno dopušteno**, a ne gdje vrijedi pravilo „ne diraj to jer oduvijek je bilo tako". Iza tog otpora, primjećuje ironično, često stoji vrlo jednostavan interes: promjena bi značila da netko mora nešto raditi, a njemu je zapravo sasvim dobro — „ja volim samo trolati na internetu". Ako tako ostane, zaključuje: „Ostajemo kultura trolova."
sections.subtitle_en: A cooperative bank that did not go through, Lithuania that succeeded, and the European fear of failure
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host talks about three unsuccessful attempts to establish a cooperative bank and about Lithuania as a fintech hub
sections.content_en:
The host offers a tangible counter-example of Croatian practice. The largest Croatian cooperative, he recounts, on three occasions attempted before the CNB to establish a bank in which the members themselves would be the owners and in which there would be no extraction from the economy — and that was not possible.

Those same people, he continues, today do the same thing through the **Central Bank of Lithuania**, which during corona consciously positioned itself as a *fintech hub* and invited everyone to come to it. From that jurisdiction, he recalls, Revolut also grew, which expanded throughout Europe and after a number of years became profitable — proving along the way that SEPA transactions can be free.

Marijana Šarolić Robić sees in this precisely what pushes entire markets forward: someone brave enough, a pioneer who dares to support such a thing. With this, she introduces a concept that, she says, the European Commissioner for Startups also speaks about — **"license to fail"**.

The problem is, she claims, in the European mentality:

- in Europe, **failure is a shame**, bankruptcy is a shame, and failure brings loss of prestige, social standing, and reputation, as well as gossip "at the lowest level";
- in America, on the contrary, they ask you how many times you have failed before they invest in you — because that means you know how to get up from your knees;
- a serial entrepreneur is not the one who made four exits, but the one who knows how to pull himself out of every situation.

Therefore, she advocates the liberalization of this paradigm: that it be permitted to experiment, fall, get up, "mess up", learn, and move on — and that Europe, and within it Croatia, position itself as a place where innovating is **socially permitted**, not where the rule applies "do not touch that because it has always been that way". Behind this resistance, she notes ironically, there often stands a very simple interest: change would mean that someone has to do some work, while he is actually doing quite well — "I just like to troll on the internet". If it remains so, she concludes: "We remain a culture of trolls."

sections.subtitle: Pet milijuna dolara po zaposleniku, data centri i 280 kilometara dalekovoda do Topuskog
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj i gošća raspravljaju o data centru u Topuskom i energetskoj infrastrukturi
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora voditelj otvara temu ekonomije umjetne inteligencije. Navodi podatak da jedna AI kompanija ostvaruje **prihod veći od pet milijuna dolara po zaposleniku** — brojku koja je, kaže, ranije bila nezamisliva za bilo kakvu inovaciju, pa i za blockchain hypeove koji su se događali. Zaključak mu je jednostavan: događa se nešto.

Druga strana te medalje je fizička. Voditelj podsjeća da je Elon Musk u Memphisu preuzeo tvornicu i u nju smjestio oko dvjesto tisuća grafičkih procesora — pa se, slikovito kaže, svi „spojimo na cloud" i zapravo trošimo struju u Memphisu. Istodobno se u Hrvatskoj, primjećuje, „na neke sumnjive načine" gradi data centar u Topuskom, uz strah da će ljudi ostati bez struje i uz odgovor tipa „pa sagradimo onda nuklearku".

Marijana Šarolić Robić dopunjuje priču konkretnim brojkama iz medija: za taj projekt navodi se potreba za **280 kilometara dalekovoda**, uz prethodnu suglasnost HEP-a. Ako ga sagrade, kaže, „svaka im čast, neka imaju što god žele imati u Topuskom". Voditelj dodaje da će to netko morati i platiti, a gošća zaključuje da dalekovode u Hrvatskoj ionako ne može podizati bilo koji d.o.o. — sve je, kaže, međusobno uvezano.

Paralelno upozorava na apsurd globalnih podjela: američki AI start-upovi, primjećuje, koriste kinesku infrastrukturu jer je *computing power* jeftiniji. „Stvaramo tu glupu dihotomiju Amerike i Europe, a de facto Kinezi trljaju ruke cijelo vrijeme", kaže, navodeći i nedavni primjer u kojem je, prema onome što je čula, za rješavanje jednog problema posegnuto za kineskim alatom. Sve to, tvrdi, ide u prilog tezi da smo **jedna ekonomija i jedna zemaljska kugla**, a da stvari koje nas dijele služe uglavnom tome da nas spriječe da inoviramo i da svijet učinimo boljim mjestom. „Nema tu neprijatelja, mi smo tu svi ljudi."
sections.subtitle_en: Five million dollars per employee, data centers, and 280 kilometers of transmission lines to Topusko
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host and the guest discuss the data center in Topusko and energy infrastructure
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the conversation, the host opens the topic of the artificial intelligence economy. He cites the data that one AI company generates **revenue exceeding five million dollars per employee** — a figure that was, he says, previously unimaginable for any kind of innovation, even for the blockchain hypes that occurred. His conclusion is simple: something is happening.

The other side of that coin is physical. The host recalls that Elon Musk took over a factory in Memphis and placed about two hundred thousand graphics processors in it — so, he says vividly, we all "connect to the cloud" and actually consume electricity in Memphis. At the same time in Croatia, he observes, "in some suspicious ways" a data center is being built in Topusko, with the fear that people will be left without electricity and with the response of the kind "well, then let's build a nuclear power plant".

Marijana Šarolić Robić complements the story with concrete figures from the media: for that project, the need for **280 kilometers of transmission lines** is stated, with prior approval from HEP. If they build it, she says, "kudos to them, let them have whatever they want to have in Topusko". The host adds that someone will have to pay for that, and the guest concludes that transmission lines in Croatia cannot be erected by just any d.o.o. anyway — everything, she says, is interconnected.

In parallel, she warns of the absurdity of global divisions: American AI start-ups, she observes, use Chinese infrastructure because *computing power* is cheaper. "We are creating that stupid dichotomy of America and Europe, while de facto the Chinese are rubbing their hands the whole time", she says, also citing a recent example in which, according to what she heard, a Chinese tool was resorted to to solve a problem. All of that, she claims, supports the thesis that we are **one economy and one globe**, and that the things that divide us serve mainly to prevent us from innovating and making the world a better place. "There are no enemies here, we are all human beings here."

sections.subtitle: Sila za dobro i za zlo: autonomni dron ili personalizirani lijek — i misliti svojom glavom
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća uspoređuje destruktivne i medicinske potencijale umjetne inteligencije
sections.content:
Voditelj sažima ambivalenciju trenutka: s umjetnom inteligencijom čovjek može biti „najbolji ikad i najgori ikad". Kao mračni scenarij navodi da praktički svatko može napraviti dron s bombom koji autonomno djeluje, sam se rekompilira i izaziva veliku destrukciju.

Marijana Šarolić Robić odmah nudi zrcalnu sliku istog *computing powera*: da se uzme kompletan medicinski zapis pacijenta i u kratkom roku napravi **personalizirani lijek za konkretan tip raka**, uzimajući u obzir obiteljsku anamnezu i dostupne lijekove — koktel koji se doslovno popije, bez kemoterapije.

Te dvije krajnosti, kaže, nisu novost. Poziva se na Russell-Einsteinov manifest iz pedeset i šeste godine: već tada je bilo jasno da čovječanstvo ima istu moć da uništi sve ili da stvori „raj na zemlji". Ljudi su, tvrdi, uvijek bili u toj poziciji — *force for good* ili *force for evil*. Novo je samo pojačanje efekta, uz marketinški proizvedeni privid da nam je „najgore ikad" i „najbolje ikad", pri čemu svaka strana forsira svoju verziju iz vlastitih razloga. Zato, zaključuje, **treba misliti svojom glavom**.

Uz obostrane zahvale, razgovor se raspliće u opuštenom tonu. Voditelj najavljuje nova gostovanja i u šali čeka kandidaturu gošće na izborima 2028., dodajući da će do tada izaći mnogi novi jezični modeli i da će „definitivno biti AI političari, ono holografija". Ističe da društvo ide prema tome da se centralizirane strukture „istope" i da dvije osobe mogu izravno razmjenjivati dobra i vrijednost. Gošća se s ograničenjima ne slaže: nitko nas, kaže, nikad nije sprječavao da razmjenjujemo krumpire i rajčice bez HNB-a. Problem, uzvraća voditelj, nastane kad se to radi obrtimice na tržištu — i to ne regulatorno, nego porezno.

Za kraj voditelj otvara još jednu temu: apsurd da je **96 posto bankarstva na hrvatskom teritoriju u stranom vlasništvu**, dok je jedini strah bankara odljev likvidnosti — pa pita zašto građanin, ako država fiskalno na silu ubire novac u zajedničku blagajnu, ne može iz tog istog proračuna posuditi novac uz kamatu. Marijana Šarolić Robić na to elegantno odgovara da je to tema za novi podcast i za sugovornika koji o njoj može govoriti s autoritetom: „Ja mogu samo lamentirati." Epizoda se zatvara zahvalama i najavom skorog nastavka.
sections.subtitle_en: A force for good and for evil: an autonomous drone or personalized medicine — and thinking with one's own head
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares destructive and medical potentials of artificial intelligence
sections.content_en:
The host summarizes the ambivalence of the moment: with artificial intelligence a human can be "the best ever and the worst ever". As a dark scenario, he mentions that practically anyone can make a drone with a bomb that operates autonomously, recompiles itself, and causes great destruction.

Marijana Šarolić Robić immediately offers a mirror image of the same *computing power*: that a patient's complete medical record be taken and in a short time **a personalized medicine for a concrete type of cancer** be made, taking into account family history and available medicines — a cocktail that is literally drunk, without chemotherapy.

These two extremes, she says, are not news. She refers to the Russell-Einstein Manifesto from the fifty-sixth year: already then it was clear that humanity has the same power to destroy everything or to create "heaven on earth". People, she claims, have always been in that position — *force for good* or *force for evil*. The only new thing is the amplification of the effect, along with the market-produced illusion that things are "worst ever" and "best ever" for us, with each side pushing its version for its own reasons. Therefore, she concludes, **one should think with one's own head**.

With mutual thanks, the conversation unwinds in a relaxed tone. The host announces new guest appearances and jokingly awaits the guest's candidacy in the 2028 elections, adding that by then many new language models will be released and that "there will definitely be AI politicians, like holography". He points out that society is moving toward centralized structures "melting away" and two people being able to directly exchange goods and value. The guest does not agree with the limitations: no one, she says, ever prevented us from exchanging potatoes and tomatoes without the CNB. The problem, the host replies, arises when this is done reversibly on the market — and that not regulatorily, but tax-wise.

In conclusion, the host opens another topic: the absurdity that **96 percent of banking on Croatian territory is in foreign ownership**, while the only fear of bankers is the outflow of liquidity — so he asks why a citizen, if the state fiscally by force collects money into a common treasury, cannot borrow money from that same budget with interest. Marijana Šarolić Robić elegantly replies to that that this is a topic for a new podcast and for an interlocutor who can speak about it with authority: "I can only lament." The episode closes with thanks and the announcement of a continuation soon.
